subject: 360 Salem Street Site Plan Review
overview: The Community Development Board continued the site plan review for 360 Salem Street to await a formal zoning interpretation on parking reductions and received a major update on the city's revised multi-year zoning reform timeline.

items.title: 360 Salem Street Public Hearing
items.summary: The board continued the public hearing for a four-story, 14-unit mixed-use building to wait for a determination from the Building Commissioner on whether the location meets high-frequency transit criteria for parking reductions. The applicant presented design revisions including a four-foot setback for fire access and Juliet balconies, while residents raised concerns about shadows on abutting properties and the reliability of local bus data.

items.title: Zoning Ordinance Amendments and ADUs
items.summary: Staff reported that residential and accessory dwelling unit (ADU) zoning amendments were withdrawn by the City Council to prioritize a new sequential process focusing on individual commercial districts. The revised timeline prioritizes Medford Square rezoning in early 2026, followed by Tufts Institutional zoning, with residential reform postponed for approximately two years.

items.title: Administrative Updates and 2026 Goals
items.summary: The board discussed setting goals for the upcoming year, including the development of design review checklists and establishing earlier deadlines for applicant document submissions. A site walk of Medford Square was suggested ahead of upcoming joint public hearings with the City Council.
